source.title: HTTP Request Tool (legacy) with Digest Auth fails with "Credentials not found"

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

The legacy HTTP Request Tool (`@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest`) cannot use a Digest Auth credential. When Generic Auth Type is Digest Auth, the tool reads the credential with the wrong type:

```ts
// packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/tools/ToolHttpRequest/utils.ts
if (genericType === 'httpBasicAuth' || genericType === 'httpDigestAuth') {
	const basicAuth = await ctx.getCredentials('httpBasicAuth', itemIndex);
```

The node stores the selected credential under `httpDigestAuth`, so `node.credentials.httpBasicAuth` is not set. The HTTP Request Tool is a full-access node type, and `_getCredentials` in `node-execution-context.ts` throws `Credentials not found` for a full-access node that requests a type it does not have. The tool never sends the request.

The HTTP Request node reads `getCredentials('httpDigestAuth', itemIndex)` for the same option. #43544 and #43617 recently added Bearer Auth and Multiple Headers Auth to this function. Digest Auth is the remaining generic type that does not work.

### To Reproduce

1. Open a workflow that has an AI Agent with the legacy HTTP Request Tool (v1 or v1.1). The node is hidden in the node panel, so use an existing workflow or import one.
2. Set Authentication to Generic Credential Type and Generic Auth Type to Digest Auth. Select a Digest Auth credential.
3. Run the agent so that it calls the tool.
4. The tool call fails with `Credentials not found`.

I did not run these steps in a running instance. I ran `NodeExecutionContext._getCredentials` from `packages/core` against `master` (`113d2c7013`), for a `toolHttpRequest` node whose `credentials` is `{ httpDigestAuth: … }`:

```
getCredentials('httpBasicAuth')  -> rejected: Credentials not found
getCredentials('httpDigestAuth') -> resolved {"user":"u","password":"p"}
```

### Expected behavior

The tool reads the `httpDigestAuth` credential and sends the request with Digest authentication (`sendImmediately: false`), as the HTTP Request node does.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code, not from a user report. A fix with a regression test follows in a PR linked to this issue.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (WSL2)

### n8n Version

`master` at `113d2c7013`

### Node.js Version

26.13.0

### Database

Not applicable: reproduced at unit level, not in a running instance

### Execution mode

Not applicable: reproduced at unit level, not in a running instance

### Hosting

self hosted (local checkout)

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `utils.ts`: the Basic/Digest branch still calls `getCredentials("httpBasicAuth", itemIndex)` for both options. The request path already keeps `sendImmediately: false` for Digest, so the credential lookup is the mismatch. Fetching with `genericType` (or selecting `httpDigestAuth` in the Digest branch) should let the existing username/password handling work for both credential types while preserving the domain check. A focused test could assert the requested credential type for each option and that Digest still sends with `sendImmediately: false`.
